intro: Białowieża is the village at the heart of the Białowieża Forest on Poland's border with Belarus, one of the last pieces of the old lowland forest of Europe. On the Żebra Żubra trail near Budy stands a great trunk with deep diamond-patterned bark, which a reader photographed from its foot and sent to us. It looks like an old ash; we would like a reader to confirm it.

trees.story:
The Białowieża Forest on the Polish-Belarusian border is one of the last pieces of the lowland forest that once covered much of Europe, and the Żebra Żubra trail, the Bison's Rib, takes walkers into it near the village of Budy. A reader photographed this trunk beside the trail with a GPS fix taken at its foot.

They stood close and pointed the camera straight up, so the photograph is almost all bark: deep, interlaced ridges running up the trunk in a diamond lattice, broad at the foot and still thick where the first limbs leave it high above. A round hollow opens in the trunk partway up, and the crown overhead is thin with autumn, its last leaves turning gold. A younger tree leans in at the edge of the frame, slight beside it.

That bark is the pattern of an old ash, but we would like a reader to confirm the species, and we have no girth or age for it. If you walk the trail, look for it, measure it if you can, and tell us here.

Stand at its foot and look up, as the reader did.

question_context: The Białowieża Forest straddles Poland's border with Belarus and is one of the last remnants of the lowland forest that once covered much of Europe. On its Polish side, the Żebra Żubra trail, the Bison's Rib, runs into the forest near the village of Budy in the Białowieża municipality. A reader walking it sent us a photograph of a trunk beside the trail, taken with a GPS fix at its foot and pointed straight up. It shows deep, interlaced ridges running up the bark in a diamond lattice, the pattern of an old ash, a round hollow partway up, and a crown thinning with autumn high above. A younger tree leans in beside it, slight by comparison. We have no species confirmation, girth or age for it yet, and no name. If you walk the trail and find it, measure it if you can and tell us on its page. Keep to the trail; parts of the forest are strictly protected.
